content: Trimethoprim is a medication prescribed to eliminate bacteria responsible for urinary tract infections. It is also used in combination with other drugs to treat specific types of pneumonia and to manage traveler’s diarrhea. It is important to note that antibiotics like trimethoprim are ineffective against colds, flu, or other viral infections. Occasionally, this medication may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Trimethoprim is available in tablet form and is taken orally, typically once or twice daily. It can be taken with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take trimethoprim exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Before taking trimethoprim, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to trimethoprim, sulfa drugs, diuretics (commonly referred to as water pills), oral diabetes medications, or any other drugs. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially phenytoin (Dilantin) and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had anemia, liver disease, or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking trimethoprim, contact your doctor immediately. Trimethoprim should be taken on an empty stomach, either one hour before or two hours after meals. However, if you experience nausea, you may take it with food. It is essential to drink at least eight glasses of liquid daily, including water, tea, coffee, soft drinks, milk, or fruit juice. If you forget to take a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Trimethoprim may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they are severe or persistent: upset stomach, vomiting, or diarrhea. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following serious symptoms: rash (hives), itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, sore throat, fever or chills, mouth sores, unusual bruising or bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, paleness, joint aches, or bluish-colored fingernails, lips, or skin. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the appropriate disposal method. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order specific lab tests to monitor your response to trimethoprim. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If you still have symptoms of infection after completing the course of trimethoprim, contact your doctor. It is crucial to maintain a written list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins, minerals, and dietary supplements. Bring this list with you to every doctor’s visit or if you are admitted to a hospital. This information is also vital in emergencies. Brand names for trimethoprim include Primsol®, Proloprim®, and Trimpex®. However, these branded products are no longer on the market, and generic alternatives may be available.
